title.title: The log-Brunn–Minkowski inequality in every dimension
title.subtitle: Claim: geometric averaging of support functions never loses volume, for origin-symmetric convex bodies

plain: Blend two shapes by a 'geometric' average of their widths: is the blend's area at least the average area?

beats.text: Two origin-symmetric bodies: a wide box $K$ and a tall box $L$, each of area 1
Average their support functions geometrically: the Wulff body is the middle square
Its area is at least $|K|^{1/2}|L|^{1/2}$ (equal here); the usual Minkowski mean is bigger

steps: Join the two bodies by a path of blended bodies
Volume along the path reduces to a variance inequality
Prove that inequality with moment coordinates and a tensor bound

achievement.label: Böröczky–Lutwak–Yang–Zhang conjecture (2012)
achievement.context: Before: the plane (BLYZ), unconditional bodies (Saroglou), local and partial-symmetry cases
achievement.note: Symmetric bodies only; equality cases not claimed

verify.detail: In Lean, in one file of about 24,000 lines. Not: the $L_p$, measure and B-conjecture corollaries
verify.ourCheck: From the paper and its Lean docs; we did not build the Lean

voice.text: Two symmetric boxes, blended geometrically. Its area never falls below their geometric mean.
Follow a path of blended bodies; volume reduces to a variance inequality.
Claimed: true for all origin-symmetric bodies, every dimension.

sources.quote: Conjectured by Böröczky-Lutwak-Yang-Zhang (Adv. Math. 2012), who proved n=2.
the Wulff body W[h_K^{1-λ} h_L^λ] has volume >= |K|^{1-λ}|L|^λ
Family 091 claims every dimension in 20 pages, and the main inequality is in Lean, in a single file of about 24,000 lines
Those corollaries are not formalized, and equality cases are not claimed.
